leads.question: Does the Monad mainnet validator binary of v0.16.5 (the package the release page names for mainnet) and the v0.16.7 binary behind rpc.monad.xyz contain the same compiled emitter as the cycle 23 harness build? Download the published packages, compare the asmjit version and the build flags (CMake options, -march, LTO) with the harness build, and disassemble the emitter functions for SHL by a non-literal, MULMOD, SAR and JUMPI to compare them with the harness object code.
leads.why: Monad runs the hot PoolManager as native x86 code in blocks, eth_call never uses that path, and every compiled-path result so far comes from a local build. An ordinary account can drive FullMath and TickMath to any edge through its own hookless pool against a pooled token, so a miscompiled block in the shipped binary would compute a wrong payout from other pools' funds.

leads.question: Carry L-1032 and L-1076 into a Polygon and BNB Chain unit. Before 8 December: is a bor tag carrying Salvador published, and does its core/vm/mulmod_memo.go, instructions.go and interpreter.go differ from v2.12.0-beta? Is a bsc tag carrying Jenner published, and does its core/vm differ from v1.8.2? After activation: rerun battery.py, targeted.py, pmdiff.py and pmdiff2.py pinned by web3_clientVersion brackets.
leads.why: Both forks land on one day, bor already adds a MULMOD memo in front of the integer library, and BNB Chain once shipped a fused comparison that always returned 0. A wrong MULMOD or comparison word changes FullMath.mulDiv for every swap, and an ordinary account chooses the inputs.

leads.question: Carry L-1075 (T14 on 8 December, T15 later). In addition, which validators of the Tempo set run binaries built with the jit feature (bin/tempo/Cargo.toml lines 267-268), and does any operator page or release note say so? If one does, transcribe the LLVM stage rules for MULMOD, SAR and JUMPI from evm2 and compare them with the specification.
leads.why: Tempo has one client. Under deferred verification from T14, a block with wrong execution can be notarized before it is verified, and a validator on a jit build runs code no endpoint answers with. A wrong arithmetic word there pays out pooled stablecoins.

leads.question: Read cycles/023/theme-monad-compiled-coverage.work/src/harness.cpp and the Monad VM varcode cache and state code it links. Is the run-to-run variance of rep1369 with a shared 3,000 account world caused by the harness host (account map, storage callbacks, router) or by Monad code? Why does case 1528 give a different native result only on the first scenario of a process?
leads.why: If either effect comes from Monad's VM, compiled or interpreted results depend on process history, which would be a consensus fault in the code that writes Monad blocks. If both come from the harness, earlier large-world runs may need a rerun.

leads.question: Transfer from the cycle 25 theme-avalanche-sae finding (Avalanche serves receipts, logs and state at latest from the answering node's own execution before settlement): on Monad, which block does eth_call at latest, safe and finalized execute against on rpc.monad.xyz, is latest a proposed block that can still be dropped, and can a receipt or balance served at latest belong to a block that never finalizes?
leads.why: Monad executes asynchronously after consensus, like the Avalanche SAE executor. Integrators that settle against latest could release funds on a state that is replaced, which the Avalanche unit examined and the Monad units did not.

leads.question: Does 0x7c5bee2a on X Layer (13,322 bytes, has an owner function) accept calls from any account and forward arbitrary calldata to the PoolManager, or only from listed senders? Read its verified source or disassemble its dispatcher, and settle the verifier's open point on the gasless finding.
leads.why: The verifier left this open. If any account can route zero-priced calls through it, block space for gasless PoolManager exits can be filled at no cost, which delays other users' withdrawals.

leads.question: Three networks are answered by PublicNode endpoints that run builds nobody published: arbitrum-one-rpc.publicnode.com (nitro vlocal+5f02f3f-modified), polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com (bor private commits, F-146) and ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com, which networks.json uses for Ethereum and which answered reth/v2.11.0-b9abbcc on 2026-11-26. Is b9abbcc the commit of the published reth v2.11.0 tag?
leads.why: Every Ethereum reference word in the opcode comparison is read from that endpoint. A modified reference would hide a difference on the other 20 networks.

leads.question: The battery runs each vector in a fresh dispatcher frame, and the script sets run the real bytecode, so repeated MULMOD with 2^256-1 then a denominator is already covered inside one frame. What no set does is alternate many different denominators and repeated identical ones across one long transaction on bor, where the memo is per EVM. Build a pmdiff script with 64 consecutive swaps over pools whose liquidity values give distinct and repeated denominators in FullMath.mulDiv (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24-48), and compare its record on Polygon with Ethereum.
leads.why: bor's MULMOD memo was cleared by reading and by short sequences. A stale reciprocal on a repeated or alternating modulus is the one stateful fault shape that an ordinary account could line up through its own pools.
